lessons.title: Truck Anatomy
lessons.subtitle: Identify the main parts of a North American tractor
notes: Cab / sleeper Driver controls and rest compartment; identify the exact vehicle and configuration before dispatching service.
Steer axle Front axle provides steering; inspect tires, steering linkage, suspension, wheel ends and brakes.
Drive axles Transmit power through differentials and axle shafts; look for leaks, abnormal noise and vibration.
Fifth wheel Tractor coupling plate that locks around the trailer kingpin; coupling integrity is safety critical.
Fuel tanks / DEF tank Diesel fuel and diesel exhaust fluid are separate; never confuse fill points.
Unit number / VIN Fleet unit ID is an internal identifier; VIN is the manufacturer-assigned vehicle identifier.

lessons.title: Engine & Cooling
lessons.subtitle: Recognize the major diesel engine support systems
notes: Engine oil Lubricates and cools moving parts; verify level and leak reports against OEM procedures.
Cooling system Radiator, coolant, water pump, thermostat, fan and hoses regulate temperature.
Turbocharger Uses exhaust energy to boost intake air; unusual whine or power loss requires diagnosis.
Belts / tensioners Drive accessories; damaged belts can disable cooling or charging.
Alternator / batteries Charge and supply electrical power; distinguish no-crank, slow-crank and charging faults.
Transmission / driveshaft Carry power to drive axles; leaks, harsh shifting and vibration require shop evaluation.

Derate Engine control may limit performance after certain faults; document dashboard messages and symptoms.

Spring parking brakes Spring force applies parking/emergency braking when air is released; never service without training.
ABS Helps control wheel lockup; warning lamps indicate a fault requiring inspection.
Low-air warning Treat as urgent; driver should follow safe stopping and operating procedures.

lessons.title: Suspension & Axles
lessons.subtitle: Load support, handling and driveline identification

Leaf springs Steel spring packs and hangers support load; cracks or displaced components are serious.
Steer / drive / trailer axle Distinguish by function, not merely by the number of wheels.
Tandem axles Two closely spaced axles that distribute vehicle weight.
Lift axle May raise when permitted and appropriate for vehicle/load configuration.
Differential Distributes torque to drive wheels; leaks and abnormal noises need inspection.
Wheel end Hub, bearings, seals and lubrication; overheating or leaking seals warrant prompt attention.

Load rating Tire and wheel capacities must meet actual axle loading and applicable requirements.
Dual tires Matched dimensions and proper inflation are important to avoid uneven load sharing.

lessons.title: Tire Wear Patterns
lessons.subtitle: Use wear patterns as clues, not final diagnoses
notes: Center wear Can indicate overinflation or operating conditions; inspect pressure history and tread.
Both shoulders Can indicate underinflation or overloading.
One-sided wear Can indicate alignment, suspension or axle issues.
Cupping / scalloping May relate to shocks, balance, wheel-end or suspension issues.
Flat spots May follow wheel lockup or extended stationary loading.
Bulge / exposed cords Potential serious tire damage; arrange qualified inspection before use.
Coordinator action Capture tire position, size, DOT tire date code, photos, tread depth and vendor findings.

lessons.title: DOT & FMCSA
lessons.subtitle: Know the inspection and recordkeeping framework
notes: DOT / FMCSA US Department of Transportation / Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.
Pre-trip inspection Driver must be satisfied the vehicle is in safe operating condition before driving.
DVIR Driver Vehicle Inspection Report; applicability and reporting rules depend on operation and defects.
Periodic inspection Most regulated commercial vehicles need qualifying periodic inspection at least every 12 months.
Roadside inspection Enforcement may inspect driver, vehicle and paperwork under applicable standards.
OOS Out of Service means operation is prohibited until relevant conditions are corrected.
Documentation Maintain inspection and repair records required by applicable rules and fleet policy.

lessons.title: Fault Codes & Lamps
lessons.subtitle: Recognize urgency without attempting remote diagnosis
notes: Check Engine / MIL Engine or emissions-related fault; capture active code and vehicle behavior.
Stop Engine / red warning Potentially severe condition; instruct driver to follow OEM safe-stop guidance.
Low oil pressure Serious engine protection warning; avoid continued operation until assessed.
High coolant temperature Overheating risk; driver should stop safely and follow manufacturer guidance.
ABS Braking control fault; service braking may remain but system needs evaluation.
DPF / DEF Aftertreatment warning; capture exact message, fluid level and derate status.
DTC / SPN / FMI Fault-code formats vary; technicians use diagnostic tools and OEM service information.

lessons.title: Breakdown Workflow
lessons.subtitle: From initial report to documented return to service
notes: 1. Triage Classify safety urgency and protect driver; call emergency services when warranted.
2. Vendor selection Find suitable mobile mechanic, tow provider or repair shop for exact equipment.
3. Confirm ETA Obtain dispatch ETA and communicate changes to operations and driver.
4. Approve scope Request diagnosis, labor estimate, parts and approval per fleet limits.
5. Monitor Track arrival, diagnosis, repair progress, parts delays and updated ETR.
6. Verify Get invoice, technician findings, test results and required compliance clearance.
7. Close Update WO, downtime, cost center and fleet/dispatch availability.

lessons.title: Real-World Scenarios
lessons.subtitle: Practice translating driver reports into next steps
notes: Scenario A: Low air warning Driver reports repeated low air warning. Confirm safe stop and location; coordinate qualified brake-system service; do not authorize continued driving.
Scenario B: Reefer high temp Record setpoint, actual temperatures, alarms, cargo type and location; escalate cargo risk and dispatch reefer specialist.
Scenario C: PM overdue Review OEM/fleet interval, last service and planned miles; arrange slot before exceeding the approved maintenance window.
Scenario D: Tire sidewall bulge Record axle and position, photo, size and location; arrange qualified tire service and assess OOS implications.
Scenario E: OOS at roadside Record inspection report, exact defects and required repairs; obtain documentation before release.
